Subject: Price guardrail + staged commitment offer for 2028 renewal

Hi Jordan / procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our notes, attached is a concise proposal that aims to: (1) lock unit pricing against market increases, (2) allow a phased prepay structure to ease cashflow, and (3) preserve flexibility for model family upgrades. High level:

- Term: 24 months (Jan 1, 2028—Dec 31, 2029)
- Commit structure: staged prepay with annual invoicing tied to usage forecast (Option A: Annual prepay for each year; Option B: 24-month single prepay with staged drawdown)
- Pricing guardrail: unit price per token for the agreed model family will not increase more than 3% YoY during the term; new model variants fall under a defined upgrade addendum (see p.2)
- Ramp credit: if actual usage in Year 1 is below forecast, remaining credit rolls forward to Year 2 with a 2% admin fee; if above forecast, overage billed at committed unit price + 15% (or at market price, whichever is lower)
- Early-sign discount: additional 3% on total committed value if contract signed by 2027-07-01

I've included a short spreadsheet with a sample annual schedule and a one-page summary (redwood-price-guardrail-2027.pdf). Please review and let me know the procurement constraints (billing/PO cadence, payment terms) so we can finalize terms.

Target for final agreement: procurement approval by 2027-07-05 to enable a 1/1/2028 effective date.

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi—

Appreciate the clear summary and the PDF. A few immediate questions from procurement / finance:

1) Cashflow: a two-year single prepay is challenging for us. We prefer annual prepay with an option to top up mid-year. Can you confirm an annual-billed variant and the exact invoicing schedule?

2) Price lock scope: does the 3% YoY guardrail apply to all models we currently use (gpt-family v1-v3) or only to the specific variants listed in the appendix? We use a mix across production and dev, and model migrations in 2028 are very likely.

3) Accounting: we need 30-day payment terms after invoice. Any billing entity issues we should be aware of?

4) If we sign early (by 7/1), will the early-sign discount apply to both years or only Year 1?

Procurement aims to have our side reviewed by 7/05, but cashflow constraints mean we might have to split Year 1 into two installments. Would Redwood entertain a split invoice (50/50) within the 12-month prepay with a small finance fee?

If you can send a clean annual-invoice option and confirm the model-upgrade treatment, we can move quickly.

Best,

Jordan—thanks, great questions. Quick answers inline below and Ben has added a technical note on model coverage.

1) Annual-billed variant: Yes — attached "proposed-annual-schedule.xlsx" contains an annual billing option with proposed invoice dates (Jan 1 each year) and a variant with two installments for Year 1 (Jan 1 and Jul 1). We can accept split Year 1 payments with a 1.5% admin fee applied to the deferred installment.

2) Price lock scope: The guardrail applies to the "agreed model family" listed in the appendix (current prod variants). For new model families or materially different architectures, we include a migration addendum. Practically: minor model upgrades (v2->v3) are covered; switching to a new architecture requires a short commercial review. Ben — any technical/ops considerations to add?

3) Payment terms: Standard is Net 30. Invoicing will be from Redwood Inc. (US entity). If your accounting needs a different invoicing entity, let us know and we can route to our billing team.

4) Early-sign discount: the 3% applies to the total committed value for the first 24-month period if signed by 2027-07-01. We'll accept procurement's 30-day payment window per request.

Ben, can you confirm the addendum language on model upgrades and whether any feature-locks are required for the price guardrail?

Thanks,
Naomi

Jordan / Naomi—quick technical note from the SE side:

- Coverage: As Naomi mentioned, guardrail covers the agreed model family (we'll enumerate the specific model IDs in the contract). Minor iterative upgrades (performance/patch releases) are included with the same unit pricing.
- New model families: If Adept adopts a materially different model (e.g., a new transformer architecture or a substantially larger context window that increases compute profile >30%), we will propose a migration commercial that either converts to the new model's unit pricing or extends the guardrail with an adjustment. We'll try to keep changes predictable and provide a 60-day notice window for any repricing.
- Usage smoothing: To help your cashflow, a stacked credit approach can be implemented: you prepay annually based on forecast; any underuse generates a rolling credit (no expiry within contract term). We can cap admin fees on deferred installments at 1.5%.

I'll attach a suggested wording snippet for the model-addendum into the redline when legal starts on it.
